title: The Peril of Dense Similarity: Why Standard RAG Fails in Contraindication and Adverse Drug Interaction Discovery
abstract: Dense embedding spaces cluster semantically related terms regardless of polarity or negated assertions. When querying complex drug-drug interactions, standard RAG retrieves sentences describing combined efficacy alongside severe contraindications without distinguishing them, causing a 16.2% adverse hallucination rate on BioASQ and ClinicalQA. We demonstrate that pure dense retrieval is hazardous in pharmacology unless combined with explicit negation and contradiction attribution engines.

sections.Abstract: Dense embedding spaces cluster semantically related terms regardless of polarity or negated assertions. When querying complex drug-drug interactions, standard RAG retrieves sentences describing combined efficacy alongside severe contraindications without distinguishing them, causing a 16.2% adverse hallucination rate on BioASQ and ClinicalQA. We demonstrate that pure dense retrieval is hazardous in pharmacology unless combined with explicit negation and contradiction attribution engines.
sections.Introduction: In clinical pharmacology, whether two drugs can be safely co-administered hinges on precise negation and conditional factors. Standard bi-encoders map 'Drug X is contraindicated with Drug Y' and 'Drug X is co-administered with Drug Y' into nearly identical vector coordinates.
sections.Methodology: We test 5 commercial and open-source RAG pipelines on 850 adverse drug interaction queries from BioASQ and MIMIC-III, measuring polarity inversion and contradiction detection.
sections.Experiments: We quantify the rate of hazardous contradictions where retrieved passages conflict with clinical consensus or where generated answers reverse contraindication guidance.
sections.Results: Standard dense RAG achieves only 68.3% accuracy on BioASQ contraindication benchmarks, generating misleading safety recommendations in 16.2% of cases due to inability to detect negative evidence. Contradiction-aware verification is mandatory to prevent dangerous clinical conclusions.
sections.Conclusion: Dense similarity is insufficient for clinical pharmacology. Safe biomedical RAG requires explicit contradiction detection and negative-evidence attribution.
